Portfolio news brief — 8 September 2026

Notable price action
- Range Nuclear Renaissance ETF (NUKZ) is +4.8% over roughly three sessions (latest observed price: $67.1300).
- Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) is -3.0% over roughly three sessions (latest observed price: $167.6950).

Market and major-name developments
- Treasury yields were little changed as investors looked ahead to inflation data due out later this week that could show how businesses and consumers are contending with higher energy costs. The key 10-year Treasury note yield — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit — was little changed at 4.788%. (CNBC)
- As markets vacillate between which way they see policymakers leaning, all eyes will turn to economic reports measuring producer and consumer prices. (CNBC)
- The Treasury Department on Tuesday sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines and a handful of other entities as part of its ongoing effort to isolate Iran's economy. The move comes as Tehran and its proxies continue to launch attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the surrounding region, further entangling other countries in the U.S.' more-than-six-month war and placing more pressure on global energy prices . (CNBC)
- Bitcoin’s hot summer has come up against Red September once again, today down close to another 1% after a monster 20% rally. It’s not alone, as macro forces weigh on markets across the board. (Decrypt)
- Here are Tuesday's biggest calls on Wall Street. (CNBC)

Meta (META)
- Meta introduced its AI personal agent app on Tuesday and is asking a subset of users to pay at a time when the company and broader artificial intelligence industry face intensifying scrutiny and public skepticism. The app, which was given the internal code name Hatch, is powered by the Muse Spark family of foundation models that Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang has been debuting at a breakneck pace since April. (CNBC)

NVIDIA (NVDA; VOO top-five holding)
- Nvidia ( NVDA -1.98% ) has delivered plenty of organic growth over its history, but acquisitions have also played a major role in its expansion from a GPU designer to a comprehensive AI platform, or factory, as CEO Jensen Huang calls it. For example, it acquired the data center networking specialist Mellanox for $6.9 billion in 2019, and it now anchors a business that generates more than $31 billion in revenue annually. (The Motley Fool)

Bitcoin (BTC)
- Strive bought another 1,375 Bitcoin last week, paying $109 million and pushing the fundraising machine behind the purchase to the edge of a ten-figure milestone. The Nasdaq-listed asset manager picked up the coins between Aug. (Decrypt)
- Strategy bought no Bitcoin in the week to September 7, a week after ending a two-month BTC purchasing drought, and spent $176.3 million buying back its own preferred stock instead, the Bitcoin treasury company said in a filing on Tuesday. All of it went on STRC, the variable rate perpetual stretch preferred, at 1,810,885 shares. (Decrypt)

Eli Lilly (LLY; XLV top-five holding)
- Eli Lilly 's ( LLY -2.28% ) success in the GLP-1 weight-loss space highlights one of the biggest risks it faces right now. And it helps explain why the company leading the GLP-1 race is working so hard to acquire smaller drugmakers to broaden its drug pipeline. (The Motley Fool)

Amazon (AMZN; VOO top-five holding)
- Qualcomm shares rose 4% on Tuesday after the company announced a data center infrastructure partnership with Amazon Web Services, a major win as the chipmaker tries to take on Nvidia in the artificial intelligence market. As part of the agreement, Qualcomm said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it issued warrants to Amazon to acquire 25 million shares in the company at $161.26 apiece for a total investment of $4 billion. (CNBC)
- Qualcomm said it’s working with Amazon across “multiple generations of customized silicon” to help build out AWS’ AI infrastructure. (CNBC)
- Qualcomm partners with Amazon to build next-generation AI data center infrastructure. (CNBC)

Informational only — verify primary sources before making investment decisions.
Routine price moves and stock-picking speculation are intentionally excluded.
